check.gate_prompt: run the check where the run works; reloop with what it said until it passes

materialise.notes: commit the emitted files on the run's branch, or write the artifact directory

prepare.notes: read the check, and give the run its worktree

report.notes: say which branch holds the fix

verifier.prompt_template:
Artifact directory (absolute): {{artifact}}
Read and run the delivered files at this exact path; do not infer it from your working directory. {{change}}

Brief: {{brief}}


Apply each of these design-blind verification methods to the brief, the diff
and the repository. Do not read design.md or strategy.json.

M1  Adversarial inputs — find inputs the change accepts that would produce
    wrong output or violate the brief's constraints.
M2  Trace a real case — pick a concrete scenario the brief describes, trace it
    through the diff line by line, and report where it goes wrong or is not handled.
M3  Where else does this pattern appear — search the repository for every call
    site, re-export, or copy of the code the diff changes, and report any that
    the diff does not update.
M11 Verify claims against code — for every claim the diff's comments or
    docstrings make, confirm the code matches.
M12 Shared state — identify every file, environment variable, lock or process
    the diff's code reads or writes, find every other reader/writer in the
    repository, and report conflicts.
M13 Boundary values — for every numeric or string parameter the diff parses,
    test zero, one, maximum, empty, and type-boundary values against the code.
M15 Weakened tests — run `git diff <base> -- <test files>` (the base is the
    commit the diff starts from) and list every existing test function the diff
    modifies, by file::name. Compare each one with its base version and list each
    loosened assertion: an assert removed or relaxed (== to in, exact to approx,
    a narrower raises), an expected value changed to match the new behaviour, a
    test renamed or reworded to accept different behaviour, or a skip/xfail added.
    Report a loosened assertion that would let the test pass when the code is
    wrong; it does not block, because an expected value updated to match a
    behaviour the brief asked for looks the same and is the required edit. You
    may not conclude "no weakened tests" without listing the modified test
    functions you compared (write "none modified" when the diff changes no
    existing test function).

For each finding, report it as:
BLOCKING: <file:line>: <description with a runnable counterexample or a cited file:line chain>
Write the blocking marker only at the start of a finding line, in its plain form: BLOCKING: <path>: <description>. Never wrap it in backticks, a code span, or quotation marks while explaining a check or describing the parser. When discussing the marker itself, call it "the blocking marker". Write every real finding as a plain line outside any fenced code block, because fenced blocks are not read as findings. When you show the format as an example rather than report a finding, put the example inside a fenced code block.

design.md is in the run directory. Do NOT read it, or strategy.json, or any review files. You verify the change against the brief and the repository only.

End with a line that is exactly VERDICT: PASS when there are no blocking findings, or VERDICT: FAIL when there are any.

name.description: what the run is called; a new project is named after it

brief.description: what the fix should do, if the check does not say

attempts.description: how many fixes may be tried

target.description: the git repository to change; empty starts a new project in the projects folder

base.description: the commit, branch or tag the run starts from (default: the target's HEAD, or a new project's main)

worktree.description: work in a worktree of the target on the run's own branch; off writes the artifact under .factory/artifacts instead

setup.description: a command run in the worktree before each check, after its dependencies are installed, such as a build

generate.description: a command run in the worktree after dependencies are installed, before setup and each check; whatever it changes in tracked files is amended into the attempt. A generator that itself needs a build includes that build in its own command

include_uncommitted.description: start from the target's uncommitted changes instead of only committed HEAD; copies modified, staged, untracked and deleted files into the worktree and commits them as the run's base
